Osteosarcoma is the most common primary: Osteosarcoma is the most common primary malignant bone tumor in children + adolescents. Bimodal age distribution: adolescent growth-spurt peak (10–20y; long-bone metaphyses) and elderly secondary peak (>60y; predominantly Paget disease-associated or post-radiation). Standard-of-care multi-modal treatment (full Indications pending): neoadjuvant chemotherapy → en-bloc surgical resection (limb-salvage preferred; amputation reserved for unresectable / vascular-bundle invasion) → adjuvant chemotherapy. MAP regimen (high-dose methotrexate, doxorubicin, cisplatin) is the global standard from EURAMOS-1 (good-responder arm). Histological necrosis ≥90% at resection predicts favorable outcome; poor responders (<90% necrosis) do NOT benefit from intensification per EURAMOS-1. Genetic relationships drive prevention-workstream surveillance: - Li-Fraumeni (germline TP53): osteosarcoma is the second-most common cancer in this syndrome; Toronto-protocol annual whole-body MRI + bone surveillance recommended. v0.2-B pilot. - Hereditary retinoblastoma (germline RB1) survivors: lifetime osteosarcoma risk markedly elevated, particularly within prior RT field. Ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor in any: Ovarian Sertoli-Leydig cell tumor in any child / adolescent / young adult should trigger DICER1 germline testing — the proportion of DICER1-positive cases is high (~30-60%, higher in younger and poorly-differentiated cases). Diagnosis in a postmenopausal woman has a lower (though non-zero) DICER1-positive yield. Treatment: fertility-sparing unilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (USO) with staging for stage IA well-differentiated tumors in young women; total hysterectomy + bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy (TAH-BSO) for postmenopausal patients or high-grade / advanced-stage disease. Adjuvant chemotherapy (BEP — bleomycin, etoposide, cisplatin — similar to germ-cell tumour regimens) for stage IC and above, or poorly-differentiated / retiform variants. Androgen excess resolves dramatically post-surgery (virilization symptoms regress but voice deepening may be permanent). Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for germline-positive survivors: contralateral ovary US q6-12 months (synchronous and metachronous DICER1-driven SLCTs reported), chest imaging (PPB risk in survivors' offspring + own residual risk), thyroid US, and abdominal-pelvic US.

PDGFRA D842V substitution mutation in advanced or metastatic GIST. The PDGFRA D842V variant accounts for approximately 6-7% of all GIST and is the most common PDGFRA exon 18 mutation (~65-70% of PDGFRA-mutant GIST). D842V confers primary resistance to imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib due to steric interference with drug binding at the activation loop. The type I kinase inhibitor avapritinib binds the active conformation of PDGFRA D842V and achieves ORR ~88% (NAVIGATOR phase 1; Heinrich CANCER DISCOV 2020) and confirmed ORR ~91% in the phase 3 NAVIGATOR expansion cohort. Imatinib is ineffective (historical ORR <10% for D842V) and must not be used as 1L for confirmed D842V-mutant GIST. Fires to route ALGO-GIST-1L step 1 to avapritinib (IND-GIST-1L- AVAPRITINIB-PDGFRA-D842V) instead of imatinib (IND-GIST-1L-IMATINIB). PDGFRA D842V substitution mutation in advanced or metastatic GIST. The PDGFRA D842V variant accounts for approximately 6-7% of all GIST and is the most common PDGFRA exon 18 mutation (~65-70% of PDGFRA-mutant GIST). D842V confers primary resistance to imatinib, sunitinib, and regorafenib due to steric interference with drug binding at the activation loop. The type I kinase inhibitor avapritinib binds the active conformation of PDGFRA D842V and achieves ORR ~88% (NAVIGATOR phase 1; Heinrich CANCER DISCOV 2020) and confirmed ORR ~91% in the phase 3 NAVIGATOR expansion cohort. Imatinib is ineffective (historical ORR <10% for D842V) and must not be used as 1L for confirmed D842V-mutant GIST. Fires to route ALGO-GIST-1L step 1 to avapritinib (IND-GIST-1L- AVAPRITINIB-PDGFRA-D842V) instead of imatinib (IND-GIST-1L-IMATINIB). NCCN GIST 2025 Category 1 preferred: avapritinib 300 mg PO QD for PDGFRA D842V-mutant unresectable/metastatic GIST. Detection: PDGFRA D842V is detectable on targeted NGS, hotspot PCR, or PDGFRA-specific IHC (D842V antibody). Tissue or ctDNA-based molecular testing of all GIST at diagnosis is standard of care per NCCN GIST 2025. PDGFRA non-D842V exon 18 mutations (e.g., D842del, DI842-843IM): intermediate imatinib sensitivity — these are NOT covered by this RF. The RF fires exclusively on the D842V substitution. Non-D842V exon 18 PDGFRA mutations route to imatinib (ALGO-GIST-1L step 2 default path).

Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (Lynch-like): colonoscopy q1-2y starting age 20-25, endometrial sampling + TVUS q1-2y from age 30-35 in women (consider earlier given higher endometrial risk than POLE), EGD q3y from age 30, urinalysis q1y from age 30. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (Lynch-like; per NCCN Genetic/Familial CRC 2025): colonoscopy q1-2y starting age 20-25, EGD q3y from age 30, endometrial sampling + TVUS q1-2y from age 30-35 in women, urinalysis annual from 30 (overlap with Lynch organ spectrum). The ultramutator phenotype in POLE-mutant tumors predicts immunotherapy benefit (high TMB) — pembrolizumab is FDA- approved for TMB-high (≥10 mut/Mb) advanced solid tumors regardless of tissue; POLE-mutant CRC and endometrial benefit appears substantial in small series. ESCAT IIA (predisposition + tumor-phenotype actionability).

PTCH1 (Patched-1) is the primary tumor s: PTCH1 (Patched-1) is the primary tumor suppressor in the Hedgehog (HH) pathway. It normally inhibits SMO by sequestering it; when HH ligand (SHH, DHH, IHH) binds PTCH1, this inhibition is released, allowing SMO to activate GLI1/2 transcription factors. Somatic PTCH1 loss is the dominant driver of sporadic BCC (~90%). Germline PTCH1 mutation causes Gorlin syndrome (Basal Cell Nevus Syndrome): multiple BCCs from early adulthood, odontogenic keratocysts, skeletal anomalies, calcified falx cerebri, and markedly increased medulloblastoma risk (SHH-subtype, predominantly desmoplastic, in childhood). Gorlin syndrome patients are exquisitely sensitive to ionizing radiation (radiation-induced BCCs within field); radiation therapy is relatively contraindicated for BCC treatment in Gorlin patients. Therapeutic implication: loss of PTCH1 in BCC justifies hedgehog inhibitor (vismodegib/sonidegib) for locally advanced/metastatic disease — routine tumor PTCH1 testing is not required because HH pathway activation is universal in BCC.

RAI is NOT effective (C-cells do not concentrate iodide). Germline RET testing is mandatory at diagnosis — drives: - Prophylactic thyroidectomy timing in kindred (MEN2B: <1 yr; MEN2A C634: <5 yr per ATA risk classification). - Pheochromocytoma screening (plasma metanephrines / urinary catechols annually) — RET drives both MTC and adrenal medullary tumors. - Hyperparathyroidism screening in MEN2A. Therapy: - Localized: total thyroidectomy + central compartment LN dissection. - Advanced / unresectable (calcitonin doubling time <1 yr or structural progression): selpercatinib (LIBRETTO-001 / -531) or pralsetinib (ARROW) for RET-mutant MTC — superior to multikinase TKIs (vandetanib ZETA / cabozantinib EXAM remain alternatives, significant toxicity). - RET-WT (RAS-mutant or other): no targeted option; cabozantinib / vandetanib by default. Basal calcitonin >10 pg/mL in MEN2 carrier → strong indication for prophylactic thyroidectomy. After thyroidectomy (prophylactic or therapeutic): post-operative calcitonin used to assess cure (<2 pg/mL = biochemical cure) and detect recurrence (q6-12 month surveillance). Autosomal-dominant inheritance with near-100% penetrance for early-childhood disease in classic SMARCB1 cases. Cancer spectrum: atypical teratoid/rhabdoid tumor (ATRT) of the CNS with infancy peak, extracranial malignant rhabdoid tumor (MRT) of kidney / liver / soft tissue, small cell carcinoma of the ovary hypercalcemic type (SCCOHT — SMARCA4 specifically), and schwannomatosis in adolescent / adult survivors. The risk window is extremely narrow (peak ATRT incidence in the first 2 years of life) so high-cadence early surveillance is non-negotiable. Prevention-persona confirmed-carrier RedFlag (§20).

Pediatric VAC + IE (Ewing-like) protocol: Pediatric VAC + IE (Ewing-like) protocols are myelosuppressive and require strict hepatic / renal monitoring in infants (often <1 yr old). LVEF threshold 55% (not 50%) in pediatric oncology reflects long-life-expectancy sensitivity to anthracycline cardiotoxicity. Larotrectinib / entrectinib much better tolerated than cytotoxic in this age group — the organ-dysfunction flag pushes harder toward TRK-inhibitor monotherapy when fusion-positive (which is >90% of cases). For TRK-inhibitor: dose by BSA / weight per FDA pediatric label; hepatic dose reduction required at bilirubin >3× ULN.
Pediatric cystic nephroma is a strong DI: Pediatric cystic nephroma is a strong DICER1-syndrome signal — diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents + siblings. Beckwith-Wiedemann syndrome is a separate (non- DICER1) etiology that shares the Wilms-spectrum abdominal-tumour surveillance protocol (abdominal US q3-4 months from birth to age 7; AFP q2-3 months from birth to age 4 — focused on hepatoblastoma). Treatment: maximal safe surgical resection (nephron-sparing partial nephrectomy when anatomically feasible; total nephrectomy if not). Histopathology after resection is critical — distinguishes pure cystic nephroma (benign-borderline, surveillance only) from cystic partially differentiated nephroblastoma (Wilms-spectrum, requires adjuvant chemo per stage) and from progression to anaplastic sarcoma of the kidney (high-grade malignant, requires multimodal therapy). Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for germline-positive survivors: chest imaging (PPB risk), abdominal-pelvic US (ovarian, Sertoli-Leydig risk in girls), thyroid US, and CNS imaging (pineoblastoma, pituitary blastoma risk under age 5).
Pediatric infection screening is broader: Pediatric infection screening is broader than adult — include CMV / herpes given immunosuppression on VAC and likelihood of reactivation in neonates / infants. HBsAg+ infants: confirm vertical transmission, consult pediatric hepatology, entecavir / tenofovir prophylaxis adapted to weight. HIV+ pediatric: ART coordination critical — TRK inhibitors (larotrectinib, entrectinib) are CYP3A4 substrates, avoid CYP3A4 inhibitors. Pneumocystis prophylaxis (TMP-SMX) is standard on cytotoxic arm. Surfaces hold via parallel pre-treatment workup.
Pediatric-inspired adolescent-young-adul: Pediatric-inspired adolescent-young-adult protocols dominate in fit <40; >65 mortality from induction toxicity is high. Mini-HCVD + inotuzumab/blinatumomab achieves better tolerability with comparable CR rates.

Pexidartinib (PLX3397), a CSF1R/KIT/FLT3 inhibitor, is FDA-approved (August 2019) for adult patients with symptomatic tenosynovial giant cell tumor (TGCT) associated with severe morbidity or functional limitations not amenable to improvement with surgery. ILLUMINATE phase III trial (Tap et al., Lancet 2019): N=120 (pexidartinib vs placebo, crossover design); primary endpoint ORR at week 25 by RECIST 1.1 and TTP-MRI. ORR: 38% (RECIST) vs 0% placebo (p<0.0001); 56% by TTP-MRI vs 0%. mDOR: not reached at median 23.1 months follow-up. Clinical benefit rate: 56%. Safety: significant hepatotoxicity (cholestatic hepatitis, including one fatal case in open-label extension); ALT/AST elevations in ~51%; FDA REMS program mandatory. EMA approved for same indication (2020). No biomarker companion diagnostic required — all TGCT patients are eligible based on clinical criteria (symptomatic, surgery-resistant). Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secr: Pheochromocytoma is a catecholamine-secreting neuroendocrine tumor of adrenal medullary origin; extra-adrenal counterparts (paragangliomas) arise from sympathetic / parasympathetic ganglia (head/neck, thoracic, abdominal). They are biologically and clinically a single spectrum (PPGL); this entity is anchored to the adrenal subset for ICD-10 cleanliness but cross-references SDHx-driven extra-adrenal paragangliomas in prevention workstream notes. Hereditary fraction is the highest known among adult cancers (~30–40%). NCCN and Endocrine Society recommend germline panel testing (RET, VHL, SDHB/C/D/AF2, NF1, TMEM127, MAX, FH) for ALL patients with PPGL — not restricted by family history. This makes PPGL a sentinel disease for hereditary cancer surveillance pathways (RET → MEN2 prophylactic thyroidectomy; VHL → multi-organ surveillance; SDHB → lifetime PPGL + RCC surveillance). Classical clinical triad: headache + palpitations + sweating; many patients present with paroxysmal or sustained hypertension. Biochemical diagnosis: plasma free metanephrines or 24-h urinary fractionated metanephrines (preferred over catecholamines). Functional imaging (MIBG, Ga-68 DOTATATE PET) for staging and...

Active moiety blocks the substance P / NK1 receptor in CNS emetic centers (nucleus tractus solitarius, area postrema), preventing the delayed phase of chemotherapy-induced nausea and vomiting (CINV) that is incompletely controlled by 5-HT3 antagonists alone. Pineoblastoma is one of the canonical em: Pineoblastoma is one of the canonical embryonal CNS manifestations of DICER1 syndrome — diagnosis in any child should trigger DICER1 germline testing regardless of family history. Distinct from pineocytoma (Grade 1, benign) and pineal parenchymal tumour of intermediate differentiation (PPTID, Grade 2-3). Treatment philosophy parallels other embryonal CNS tumours: maximal safe surgical resection (gross total resection is prognostically dominant); craniospinal irradiation in age-appropriate patients (deferred under age 3 due to neurocognitive toll); adjuvant high-dose chemotherapy regimens (often COG/SIOP protocols with carboplatin, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, cisplatin, etoposide combinations + autologous stem-cell rescue in high-risk cases). Trilateral retinoblastoma (bilateral RB1-carrier with pineal pineoblastoma) historically had near-uniform mortality; modern MRI surveillance from RB1-carrier diagnosis has shifted some cases to earlier detection with improved outcomes.

Piperacillin is a ureidopenicillin that: Piperacillin is a ureidopenicillin that binds penicillin-binding proteins (PBPs) and inhibits bacterial cell-wall synthesis, producing rapid bactericidal activity against most Gram-negative bacilli including Pseudomonas aeruginosa, most Enterobacterales, many anaerobes, and selected Gram-positive cocci. Tazobactam is an irreversible β-lactamase inhibitor (penicillanic acid sulfone) that binds and inactivates plasmid-mediated and chromosomal class A β-lactamases (TEM, SHV, CTX-M ESBLs partially), restoring piperacillin activity against many β-lactamase-producing organisms. First-line empiric monotherapy for febrile neutropenia (FN) at most centers per IDSA, ECIL-4, and NCCN guidelines because of pseudomonal coverage, anaerobic activity, and good safety profile.

Pituitary blastoma is the strongest sing: Pituitary blastoma is the strongest single-tumour DICER1-syndrome signal — diagnosis in any infant should immediately trigger DICER1 germline testing AND cascade-testing of parents (>95% pituitary blastomas carry pathogenic germline DICER1). Distinct from far-more- common pituitary adenomas (which are not DICER1-driven and are typically adult-onset). Treatment: trans-sphenoidal or trans-cranial resection (technically challenging in infants — pituitary blastomas are bleeding-prone and locally invasive); adjuvant chemotherapy (carboplatin-VP16-cyclophosphamide-based regimens reported in case series); RT generally avoided under age 3 due to severe neurocognitive + endocrine toll. Hypercortisolism management (medical adrenal blockade, sometimes adrenalectomy) is an essential pre-operative bridge. Lifelong endocrine replacement (hydrocortisone, growth hormone, thyroid, gonadal axis) after curative-intent resection. Lifelong DICER1-syndrome surveillance for survivors.

Treatment by type: Type I — complete surgical resection; close follow-up imaging for new cysts or solid transformation. Highly lipid-soluble — penetrates CNS readily (CSF levels ~100% of plasma), the basis of its central role in PCNSL induction (MATRix), CNS-relapse-risk lymphoma conditioning (TBC = thiotepa + busulfan + cyclophosphamide; TT-BCNU), and intrathecal use for leptomeningeal disease.

Potent ATP-competitive small-molecule in: Potent ATP-competitive small-molecule inhibitor of all three AKT serine/threonine kinase isoforms (AKT1, AKT2, AKT3) within the PI3K-AKT-mTOR signaling pathway. FDA approval Nov 2023 (mutation-restricted).

Risk stratification by SITC 2021: - **Low risk** (generally safe to proceed with monitoring): thyroiditis, vitiligo, stable psoriasis, type 1 diabetes — irAE flare mild, manageable. - **Moderate risk** (proceed with specialist input): RA, IBD (Crohn/UC), sarcoidosis, sicca syndrome, psoriatic arthritis — flare rate ~50%; baseline DMARDs often OK to continue (methotrexate, HCQ but NOT high-dose steroids or anti-TNF at start). - **High risk** (strongest caution; consider alternative if available): active autoimmune hepatitis, myasthenia gravis, inflammatory myopathy, neuromyelitis optica — flare can be life-threatening; benefit-risk discussion mandatory. Pulmonary sarcoidosis specifically: ICI-induced sarcoid-like reactions are well-documented (5-7% of patients on ICI), often mimicking disease progression on imaging. Preferred 5-HT3 antagonist for HEC and f: Preferred 5-HT3 antagonist for HEC and for multi-day chemotherapy regimens because of long half-life and demonstrated superiority in delayed-phase CINV control vs ondansetron in head-to-head trials (Saito 2009, Aapro 2014). Triple antiemetic regimen for HEC: NK1 antagonist (aprepitant or fosaprepitant) + palonosetron 0.25 mg IV + dexamethasone 12 mg IV day 1, with dex tapered through delayed phase. Akynzeo (netupitant 300 mg + palonosetron 0.5 mg) fixed-dose oral capsule simplifies triple therapy to two pills (Akynzeo + dex) on day 1. Lowest QT signal in 5-HT3 class — preferred when ondansetron contraindicated due to QT concerns or cardiac comorbidity. Minimal CYP-mediated metabolism makes it the safer 5-HT3 choice in polypharmacy patients (e.g., patients on CYP3A4 inhibitors).
Preferred BTKi for CLL 1L per NCCN 2025: Preferred BTKi for CLL 1L per NCCN 2025 (over ibrutinib due to less cardiac toxicity). ELEVATE-TN (1L CLL): superior PFS vs Clb+O at 5y; ELEVATE-RR (r/r): non-inferior to ibrutinib with better safety. Funding pathway must be confirmed pre-start in Ukraine.
Preferred BTKi over ibrutinib in modern: Preferred BTKi over ibrutinib in modern CLL/MCL guidelines (ELEVATE-RR for r/r CLL — comparable efficacy, fewer cardiac/hypertension events). ELEVATE-TN: 1L CLL data also favorable. Ukraine: registered but NOT reimbursed via NSZU — funding…

Effect is stronger in high-incidence populations and in younger individuals where atrophic gastritis / intestinal metaplasia has not yet developed. Evidence for H. pylori → gastric MALT lymphoma: eradication is the first-line treatment for early-stage gastric MALT lymphoma, with Wotherspoon regression in ~70-80% of cases (especially t(11;18)- negative). This is treatment-persona territory (existing MALT lymphoma in setting of confirmed H. pylori → treatment Indication, not yet authored) — distinct from prevention persona (chronic H. pylori → prevent MALT/adenocarc...

Prevention-persona RedFlag (CHARTER §3 amended 2026-05-18 Path A, HCP-mediated). Fires when patient profile shows chronic HCV (HCV-RNA detectable OR HCV-Ab+ with persistent viremia >6 months) AND no confirmed B-cell NHL diagnosis. Engine routes such patients to a PreventionPlan recommending DAA antiviral therapy (per IND-CHRONIC-HCV-PREVENTION-DAA) as the etiological-cancer-prevention pathway. Evidence for HCV → NHL causation (IARC Group 1): multiple cohort studies show 2-3x increased risk of indolent B-cell NHL in chronic HCV carriers; epidemiology especially robust for MZL subtypes. DAA cure (SVR12) has been associated with reduced NHL incidence in post-treatment cohorts (de-Re et al. and others) and with regression of established HCV-associated indolent NHL (the basis of IND-HCV-MZL-1L-ANTIVIRAL for the treatment persona). This is a STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode exemption (sources cited, draft flag set). Prevention-persona RedFlag for EBV-drive: Prevention-persona RedFlag for EBV-driven cancer prevention in immunocompromised hosts. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Gating by additional immunocompromise context is deliberate — EBV seroprevalence is >90% in immunocompetent adults globally, so a RF triggered on EBV alone would fire universally and provide no clinical signal.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for FAMMM / C: Prevention-persona RedFlag for FAMMM / CDKN2A. STUB odottaa kahden Co-Lead-ehdokkuutta.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HBV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HBV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on HBsAg+ OR detectable HBV-DNA in patient without HCC. HBV-associated DLBCL/NHL is also documented in literature but with weaker effect-size data than the HCV-NHL link; covered via the broader NHL prevention surveillance bullet in the antiviral indication rationale. Distinct from RF-UNIVERSAL-HBV-REACTIVATION-RISK (existing) which is the treatment-time RF for HBV reactivation during anti-CD20 / chemo.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HCV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than either mono-infection RF — coinfection carries documented synergistic HCC risk AND DAA-cure-induced HBV reactivation risk that requires combination antiviral. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending concurrent DAA + nucleos(t)ide analog + intensified HCC surveillance (US + AFP q4-6mo, more frequent than the q6mo cadence for either mono-infection). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. NHL prevention (HCV-driven) continues to be a secondary benefit; tracked via prose in the combined-antiviral indication rationale. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HCV-NHL-PREVENTION-OPPORTUNITY and RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence over the two individual RFs (higher priority).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-dri: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HHV-8-driven malignancy prevention. Fires on HHV-8 seropositivity in HIV+, transplant, or other immunocompromised host without confirmed Kaposi sarcoma / MCD / PEL. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending immune restoration (ART for HIV+; transplant-immunosuppression rebalance) + mucocutaneous + oral + GI / lymph-node surveillance. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-KAPOSI. MCD and PEL are HHV-8-driven but not yet authored as distinct Disease entities — covered via the prose surveillance rationale in the indication for now. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (existing) — that is HIV-as-RF; this is HHV-8-positivity-as-RF (the co-factor that turns HIV-related immunocompromise into Kaposi risk specifically).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HIV + HBV coinfection cancer prevention. Higher severity (critical) than mono-infection HBV RF — coinfection carries documented accelerated-fibrosis + elevated HCC risk AND a hard constraint on antiviral selection (tenofovir-based ART mandatory; entecavir monotherapy contraindicated). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending tenofovir-based ART (covers both viruses simultaneously) + AASLD HCC surveillance q6mo. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-HCC. HIV-driven AIDS-defining malignancies (Kaposi sarcoma via HHV-8 reactivation, NHL, cervical) are covered separately via RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HHV8-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION. Distinct from RF-CHRONIC-HBV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION and RF-CHRONIC-HIV-MALIGNANCY-PREVENTION (individual mono-infection RFs). When coinfection trigger fires, this RF takes precedence (higher priority) and the indication enforces tenofovir-based ART selection.

Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending durable ART suppression (per IND-CHRONIC-HIV-PREVENTION-ART) + cancer screening cadence (annual anal cytology in MSM/HIV+; q3-yearly cervical Pap in WLHIV; opportunistic Kaposi/oral hairy leukoplakia visual screening). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS as the canonical HIV-associated NHL. KS, cervical, anal, Hodgkin, HCC are also HIV-associated; covered via screening recommendations in the ART indication rationale rather than discrete Disease anchors (until DIS-KAPOSI etc. land in v0.2-A authoring backlog).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPRC. STU: Prevention-persona RedFlag HPRC:lle. STUB odottaa kahden joukkueen johtoa.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-assoc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HPV-associated cancer prevention. Fires on persistent high-risk HPV positivity OR incomplete/absent vaccination in age-eligible individual. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending vaccination (Gardasil-9) and/or risk-group-appropriate screening cadence (cervical: USPSTF Pap+HPV co-test q5y ages 30-65; anal: HRA + cytology q1y in MSM/HIV+/post-transplant). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CERVICAL and DIS-ANAL-SCC. Oropharyngeal squamous cell carcinoma and vulvar/vaginal/penile not yet in KB — v0.2-A authoring backlog.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for HTLV-1-dr: Prevention-persona RedFlag for HTLV-1-driven ATLL prevention. Unlike HCV/HBV/H. pylori, there is no curative regimen — the intervention is surveillance + transmission prevention, not cure. STUB pending Co-Lead review. Geographic context: HTLV-1 endemic regions include Japan (southwest), Caribbean basin, parts of sub-Saharan Africa, parts of South America, Middle East. Ukraine is low-prevalence; this RF is more relevant for diaspora patients or those with travel/origin from endemic regions.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 the: Prevention-persona RedFlag for I-131 therapeutic-dose lifetime cumulative exposure. Surveillance: CBC q12mo for leukemia signal (sensitivity modest); breast surveillance per general-population USPSTF unless additional risk factors; oral + salivary symptom awareness. Highest-impact preventive intervention is hydration + lemon-juice sialagogue during I-131 administration (reduces salivary gland uptake) — retrospectively non-actionable for prior exposure. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for MASLD/NAF: Prevention-persona RedFlag for MASLD/NAFLD HCC risk. Cirrhotic MASLD meets AASLD HCC-surveillance threshold (US ± AFP q6mo). Non-cirrhotic advanced fibrosis is a gray zone — closer hepatology follow-up but not yet routine surveillance. Major actionable lever: weight loss + cardiometabolic management. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confi: Prevention-persona RedFlag for NF1 confirmed-carrier / clinical- diagnostic-criteria-met cohort. Multi-organ surveillance: pediatric ophthalmology q6-12mo to age 8 (optic glioma); whole-body MRI for MPNST surveillance + symptom-driven biopsy of growing/painful/ neurologically-symptomatic plexiform neurofibromas; women: annual mammography from age 30, MRI from age 30-50. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverr: Prevention-persona RedFlag for O. viverrini-driven cholangiocarcinoma prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifelong hepatobiliary surveillance (US + CA 19-9 q12mo from age 40 in heavily-exposed cohorts). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-CHOLANGIOCARCINOMA. Northeast Thailand has the world's highest cholangiocarcinoma incidence (up to 90 per 100K) — attributable fraction in endemic regions exceeds 50%. Geographic context: relevant for Mekong-region diaspora, refugees, travelers, and adoptees. Companion to RF-CLONORCHIS-CHOLANGIO-PREVENTION (East Asian liver-fluke pathway, biologically similar mechanism).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PALB2 het: Prevention-persona RedFlag for PALB2 heterozygous carriers. PALB2 approaches BRCA2 breast-cancer penetrance and warrants BRCA-style surveillance with annual breast MRI + mammography from age 30, plus pancreatic surveillance (EUS or MRI alternating annually from age 50, or 10 years before earliest PDAC in family) for FDR-of-PDAC carriers per CAPS consortium 2022. RRSO discussion deferred to BRCA-style threshold given lower ovarian penetrance. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for PCOS-anov: Prevention-persona RedFlag for PCOS-anovulation endometrial risk. Separated from the broad reproductive RF for clearer routing — PCOS- specific counseling (progestin restoration, metformin, weight loss) is distinct from generic reproductive-history counseling. Symptom-driven endometrial biopsy in any abnormal bleeding ≥6 months of amenorrhea pre-menopausal OR any post-menopausal bleeding. STUB pending two-Co- Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RA: Prevention-persona RedFlag for RAD51C/RAD51D heterozygous carriers. Approaches BRCA-level ovarian penetrance — NCCN endorses RRSO at completed childbearing or age 45-50. Breast surveillance: individualised by family history; consider annual MRI in additional- risk subset. Olaparib PARP inhibitor active in RAD51C/D-mutant established ovarian cancer (PROfound + GEN-ALL trials). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haemat: Prevention-persona RedFlag for S. haematobium-driven bladder SCC prevention. Fires on any documented exposure history with confirmatory testing. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending praziquantel (if active infection) + lifetime urinary surveillance (urinalysis q6-12mo, cytology + cystoscopy for any new hematuria). STUB pending Co-Lead review. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-UROTHELIAL. S. haematobium-driven bladder cancers are predominantly SCC histology (distinct from urothelial / transitional cell carcinoma that dominates Western cohorts) — engine surfaces this distinction in the prevention rationale prose. Geographic context: Ukraine is non-endemic; this RF is relevant for patients with diaspora / refugee / travel / origin history from sub-Saharan Africa, Egypt, Sudan, Yemen, parts of South America.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for SDH-defic: Prevention-persona RedFlag for SDH-deficiency syndrome. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for active to: Ennaltaehkäisyhenkilö RedFlag aktiiviseen tupakkakäyttöön. Suurimman vaikutuksen omaava, syövän riskitekijäin interventio. Moottorireitit PreventionPlaniin suosittelevat strukturoitua lopettamisneuvontaa + lääkehoitoa + LDCT-keuhkoseulontaa, jos USPSTF-testi on mahdollinen. STUB odottaa kahden kliinisen ja kliinisen ryhmän välisen johtajan eroa CHARRTER-ohjelman 6.1 §:n dev-moodia.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for anthracyc: Prevention-persona RedFlag for anthracycline cumulative dose ≥250 mg/m². Cardio surveillance focus (HF / cardiomyopathy); t-AML surveillance overlap covered by separate RF-IATROGENIC-TOPO2-TAML-PREVENTION. Echo q1-5y depending on risk profile (ASCO/COG-LTFU cadence). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending baseline + serial echo + BNP. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for aromatic-: Prevention-persona RedFlag for aromatic-amines → urothelial bladder cancer prevention. Fires on documented occupational exposure. DIS-UROTHELIAL anchor preferred but using DIS-HCC as fallback if not in KB on this branch. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic E: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ETS exposure (household / workplace ≥10y). IARC Group 1 + US Surgeon General-confirmed cause of lung cancer in non-smokers. risk_category=occupational is closest enum match — schema lacks an explicit 'environmental' enum. Distinct from active-smoking RF. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending exposure elimination (cohabitant smoking cessation / workplace smoke-free policy enforcement / personal mitigation) + USPSTF screening eligibility check + symptom-triggered evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic P: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic PPI exposure ≥10y. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) indication-review + de-prescription where the PPI is no longer needed (most common scenario), (2) fasting gastrin + chromogranin A in cohort with persistent acid-suppression indication, (3) EGD with body/fundus biopsies in those with elevated gastrin or symptoms; surveillance EGD q3-5y if atrophic gastritis or ECL hyperplasia documented. Anchored to DIS-GASTRIC (gastric NET and atrophic-gastritis-derived adenocarcinoma both gastric-body diseases); NET-specific outcomes carried in indication prose. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic a: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic anti-TNF biologic exposure ≥3y in pediatric / adolescent / young-adult IBD cohort. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) EBV serology baseline in young adults, (2) B-symptom + lymphadenopathy awareness, (3) annual skin examination (synergistic with concomitant thiopurine + UV), (4) periodic shared-decision discussion of combination- therapy step-down where IBD activity allows (anti-TNF monotherapy has favourable cancer signal vs combination with thiopurine), (5) vaccination catch-up (HPV, HBV, influenza, pneumococcal). Severity = minor — absolute attributable risk in anti-TNF monotherapy is small; the meaningful signal is the combination- with-thiopurine HSTCL warning specifically in pediatric / young- adult cohort, addressed via combination-step-down counseling. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS + DIS-HSTCL. STUB pending two-Clinical- Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic i: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic inorganic arsenic exposure via drinking water >10 µg/L (WHO + US EPA MCL). IARC Group 1 carcinogen with established urothelial, lung, and non-melanoma skin cancer etiology. Anchored to DIS-UROTHELIAL per task brief; lung + skin surfaced via relevant_diseases. risk_category=occupational is closest enum match. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending water source change / filtration + intensified screening for affected organs. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic o: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic occupational outdoor UV exposure ≥10y in high-UV-index latitudes. IARC Group 1 solar UV. Distinct from broader RF-LIFESTYLE-UV-EXPOSURE-PREVENTION (which covers tanning beds + sunburn history + recreational UV). Anchored to DIS-BCC per task brief (closest skin DIS to UV-NMSC). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending photoprotection counseling + clinical skin exam cadence + patient skin self-exam education + Vitamin D balance. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic p: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic pancreatitis → PDAC. Hereditary pancreatitis carries highest risk (~40-50% lifetime). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic r: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic residential PM2.5 >35 µg/m³ annual average (WHO 2021 IT-1). IARC Group 1 outdoor air pollution + PM. Population-attributable fraction modest individually but large absolute burden in high-exposure regions including industrial Ukraine + during war-related fire / debris events. risk_category=occupational is the closest enum match — schema lacks an explicit 'environmental' enum (§20 ratification pending). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending exposure reduction + USPSTF lung-cancer screening eligibility + symptom-triggered evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ≥: Prevention-persona RedFlag for chronic ≥3y post-transplant immunosuppression cohort. Engine routes to PreventionPlan with long-cycle surveillance cadence appropriate to the chronic cohort (vs the acute-window EBV-DNA cadence in the new-transplant RF). Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-TRANSPLANT-IMMUNOSUPPRESSION- PREVENTION (which covers acute / new-transplant window). Both RFs may fire simultaneously in the early-chronic window (1-3y post-transplant) — engine routes to both surveillance tracks, render layer deduplicates overlapping recommendations. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS as the primary lymphoma anchor (late- onset PTLD histology more DLBCL-like; DIS-PTLD as the canonical early-onset EBV-driven entity). Multiple cancer types listed in relevant_diseases reflect the broad cumulative-risk profile of the chronic cohort. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for combined: Prevention-persona RedFlag for combined HRT exposure ≥5y. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) shared-decision discussion of risk-benefit (vasomotor symptoms, bone-density preservation vs breast / VTE / cardiovascular risks), (2) lowest-effective-dose + shortest-duration principle per NAMS / ACOG, (3) breast surveillance per USPSTF cadence — supplemental imaging not recommended on HRT alone (density-related supplemental imaging is a separate axis), (4) symptom-prompted endometrial workup (any abnormal bleeding → TVUS + biopsy) for women on sequential/cyclic combined or with intact uterus on any HRT, (5) annual GYN exam. Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-TAMOXIFEN-ENDOMETRIAL-PREVENTION (different mechanism: SERM with partial endometrial agonism). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

IARC:n yhdistetty signaali D-vitamiinista. RCT-todisteet lisälääkkeestä sekoittuvat väestöannoksiin – neuvonta korostaa riittävää saantia/replektiota, ei farmakologista annostelua. Moottorireitit ehkäisysuunnitelmaan suosittelevat ruokavalion neuvontaa + D- vitamiinireplectionia + CRC-seulontaa USPSTF:ää kohti. STUB odottaa kahden klinikin ja Co-Lead-seulan välistä eroa CHARRER:n §6.1 dev-moodia kohti.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for cumulativ: Prevention-persona RedFlag for cumulative hormonal-contraception exposure ≥10y, iatrogenic-axis only (exposure-as-risk). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending HPV co-test on schedule per ASCCP / USPSTF, age-appropriate mammographic screening per USPSTF, attentive symptom history (breast lump, abnormal bleeding). Severity minor — absolute risk increment small, effect on breast cancer attenuates after stop. Distinct from RF-REPRODUCTIVE-OCP-LONG-TERM (balanced risk-benefit counseling, see §20 reproductive bucket). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for endometri: Ennaltaehkäisyhenkilö RedFlag endometrioosiin liittyvän munasarjasyövän riskin varalta. CA-125 + TVUS-hoitovälinettä ei ole olemassa (ei suositella yleis- tai endometriosiseulontaan NCCN/USPSTF-valmistetta kohti). Neuvoo: oiretietoisuus; harkitsee riskin vähentämistä salpingektomian yhteydessä, kun lapsi on syntynyt, tai hysterektomiaa hyvänlaatuisten käyttöaiheiden varalta; BSO on varattu niille, joilla on muita riskitekijöitä. STUB odottaa kahden Co-Lead -merkin antamista CARTER-tilaa kohden §6.1 dev-muotoa.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for heavy alc: RedFlag-lääkehenkilö raskaan alkoholin käyttöön. PreventionPlanin moottorireitit suosittelevat strukturoitua lopettamis-/koordinointineuvontaa + lääkehoitoa + asianmukaista syöpäseulontaa (ruokatorven endoskopia suuren riskin varalta, rintasyöpäseuranta naisille). STUB odottaa kahden kliinisen ja kliinisen ryhmän välistä eroa CHARTER-mallissa 6.1 dev-moodissa.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for high cumu: Ennaltaehkäisyhenkilö RedFlag suuren UV-altistuksen varalta. IARC Group 1 -luokitus parkitusvuoteille (2009). NCCN Melanooma + AAD -ohjeet tukevat UV:n suojausneuvontaa + ihon itsekokeilua + kliinistä ihon tenttikoetta. Moottorireitit PreventionPlaniin suosittelevat aurinkosuojaa  sekä ihon seurantaa. STUB odottaa kahden klinikon leikkausta, joka on voimassa per CHARRTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for high-pari: Prevention-persona RedFlag for high-parity cervical risk amplifier in HPV-positive women. Counseling: adherence to cervical screening per USPSTF/WHO age-and-method schedule; catch-up HPV vaccination through age 45 per ACIP shared-decision; smoking cessation (synergistic risk). STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for in-utero: Prevention-persona RedFlag for in-utero DES exposure. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending annual gynecologic exam with speculum + bimanual + careful palpation of vaginal walls (specific technique for DES daughters per ACOG), colposcopy with vaginal + cervical staining for early detection of CCA, cervical cytology / HPV co-test on routine cadence, breast surveillance per age- appropriate USPSTF cadence. Cohort is aging — bimodal-risk window extends past 40y; surveillance does NOT stop at any age cutoff. Cancer scope: anchored to DIS-VULVAR-VAGINAL-SCC (closest existing Disease entity for vaginal-tract anchor) + DIS-CERVICAL. DES- associated cancer is histologically clear-cell adenocarcinoma — NOT yet authored as a distinct DIS-VAGINAL-CLEAR-CELL entity; histology-specific surveillance considerations carried via the indication prose. Future authoring of DIS-VAGINAL-CLEAR-CELL recommended. Distinct from RF-IATROGENIC-LONG-TERM-HRMNL-CONTRACEPTION- PREVENTION (post-natal hormonal exposure, exposure-as-cofactor). This is a one-time in-utero developmental exposure — surveillance cohort is closed (no new DES daughters); known existing cohort remains at lifelong elevated risk.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for late-firs: Prevention-persona RedFlag for late-first-pregnancy + short-breastfeeding combination. Modest individual effect sizes; cumulative effect non-trivial. Cannot retroactively modify primary trigger (timing of reproductive events) — counseling is forward-looking (encourage breastfeeding when feasible in subsequent pregnancies) + tightened breast cancer screening. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term: Prevention-persona RedFlag pitkäaikaiseen yhdistettyyn OCP-käyttöön ≥10-vuotiaat. Sekalainen syöpäprofiili – vaatimaton riskiprofiilin nousu (rinta, kaulan ja kaulan alueen välinen HPV) JA merkittävä suojaus (munasarja, endometriumi). Moottorireitit PreventioPlan-suunnitelmaan suosittelevat COUNSELING-BALANCE-aiheista, ei yksipuolista riskivaroitusta. Kriittinen, joka tekee kerroksesta täydellisen riski-hyötypaneelin. STUB odottaa kahden kliinisen Co-Lead-merkin eroa CHARTER-tilaa kohden 6.1 dev-mode.

Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term low-dose MTX exposure (RA, psoriasis, IBD). Surveillance: low-threshold workup for unexplained lymphadenopathy, B-symptoms, organomegaly, mass — MTX withdrawal + observe 8-12 weeks first (~50% regress); persistent → DLBCL-style workup. Skin examination annually. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term ≥3y thiopurine (azathioprine / 6-MP) exposure. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) annual whole-body skin exam by dermatologist + aggressive sun-protection counseling, (2) EBV serology baseline check in young adults pre-initiation (avoid initiation in EBV-seronegative young men per ECCO 2019), (3) annual B-symptom + lymphadenopathy review, (4) shared-decision discussion of indication continuation vs alternatives (MTX for RA, biologics for IBD) at year 5, (5) HPV vaccination catch-up where applicable. Anchored to DIS-DLBCL-NOS (lymphoma) + DIS-BCC (closest skin-cancer anchor for SCC and BCC). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.

Prevention-persona RedFlag for long-term ≥5y calcineurin-inhibitor exposure (cyclosporine or tacrolimus). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending (1) annual or q6mo whole-body skin exam by dermatologist (q6mo if any prior skin cancer), (2) aggressive sun-protection counseling, (3) HHV-8 awareness in endemic cohorts + KS surveillance (skin, oral, GI), (4) HPV vaccination catch-up if transplant context, (5) shared-decision discussion with transplant team of switch to mTOR inhibitor (sirolimus / everolimus) in patients with cumulative skin- cancer burden — CONVERT + ProSparc evidence: mTOR-switch reduces new SCC. Anchored to DIS-KAPOSI + DIS-BCC. Distinct from broader RF-IATROGENIC-TRANSPLANT-IMMUNOSUPPRESSION-* RFs by drug-class specificity — applies also to non-transplant calcineurin-inhibitor users (psoriasis, atopic dermatitis, nephrotic syndrome). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for low Medit: Prevention-persona RedFlag, jolla on matala ruokavalion ruokavalion ja ruokavalion välinen suhde. Väkilukutason ruokavalion muotoinen vipu – erottumassa yksiravinneravitsemuksista (kuitu, kalsium, punainen liha). PREDIMED RCT (2013 ensisijainen päätetapahtuma kardiovaskulaarinen; vuoden 2015 toissijainen CRC-analyysi) + EPIC + NHS-tarkkuussignaali. Ankkuroitunut DIS-CRC:lle, koska kuviosyöpä on vahvin näyttö siellä; monisyöpähyöty perustuu perusteluihin. Moottorireitit PreventionPlan -ohjelmaan suosittelevat ruokavalion ja mallin mukaista neuvontaa + USPSTF-cadence seulontaa ankkuria kohti. STUB odottaa kahden klinikan ja yhtymän välistä eroa CHARRTER-ohjesäännön 6.1 §:n dev-moodissa.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for low dieta: Prevention-persona RedFlag for low dietary fibre intake (<15 g/day). WCRF/AICR convincing-evidence rating for CRC. Effect size modest individually but population-attributable fraction non-trivial (low fibre intake is endemic in Western diets). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending dietary counseling + USPSTF-cadence CRC screening. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for obesity (: Prevention-persona RedFlag lihavuuden hoitoon (BMI ≥ 30). Preventiosuunnitelman moottorireitit suosittelevat rakenteellista painonpudotustoimenpidettä + bariatrista leikkauskeskustelua luokan 2/3 lihavuuden ja syövän seulonnan yhteydessä BMI:n nostamaa riskiprofiilia kohti. STUB odottaa kahden potilaan leikkausta.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior alk: Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior alkylator chemotherapy exposure. Median t-AML latency 5-7y post-exposure; cumulative incidence ~1-10% at 10y. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending CBC q3-6mo for first 10y post-chemo + low threshold for marrow evaluation if cytopenias appear. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior the: Prevention-persona RedFlag aiemmalle terapeuttiselle säteilylle.Lapsissyöpä Selviytyminen + LATE-konsortioasiakirja kasvatti toisen ensisijaisen pahanlaatuisen syövän riskiä vuosikymmeniä RT:n jälkeen. STUB odottaa kahden ehdokkaan eroa.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior top: Prevention-persona RedFlag for prior topoisomerase-II inhibitor exposure. Distinct from alkylator t-AML: shorter latency (2-3y vs 5-7y), characteristic 11q23/21q22 cytogenetics, often APL-like t(15;17). Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending CBC q3mo for first 5y post-chemo + low threshold for marrow evaluation. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode. Note: anthracycline exposure also fires RF-IATROGENIC-ANTHRACYCLINE-CARDIO-PREVENTION (separate cardio + t-AML surveillance overlap).
Prevention-persona RedFlag for processed: Prevention-persona RedFlag for processed-meat consumption ≥50g/day. WCRF/AICR convincing evidence + IARC Group 1 classification for CRC. Effect size modest individually but population-attributable fraction non-trivial. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending dietary counseling + CRC screening per USPSTF. STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for refractor: Prevention-persona RedFlag resistentille keliakialle → EATL-ehkäisy. Palot jatkuvassa villousatrofiassa / poikkeavassa IEL-klonaaliteetissa / RCD2-ominaisuuksissa. STUB odottaa kahta klinikkoa, jotka ovat saaneet leimansa Clinical-Co-Lead -elokuvasta per Charter §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for reproduct: Ennaltaehkäisevä henkilö RedFlag lisääntymis-historiallisille riskitekijöille. Vaikutuskoot ovat vaatimattomat yksilökohtaisesti mutta kumulatiiviset. STUB odottaa kahden ryhmän johtajaa.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for salt/pick: Prevention-persona RedFlag for salt/pickle-heavy diet. Counseling: reduce to WHO <5 g/day; co-test for H. pylori in high-intake + high-prevalence settings (Eastern Europe, East Asia); diet-quality intervention (Mediterranean / DASH patterns) provides additional cardiovascular benefit. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for sedentary: Ennaltaehkäisyhenkilö RedFlag istuma- ja liikuntaesteisiin. WCRF/AICR vakuuttavat todisteet CRC:lle + endometriumille + postmenopausaaliselle rintasyövän suojaukselle. Moottorireitit PreventionPlan -suunnitelmaan suosittelemassa rakenteellista liikuntaneuvontaa HHS:n ja ACS:n ohjeissa. STUB odottaa kahden kliinisen yhteiskuvan hyväksyntää per CHARRER §6.1 dev-muoto.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for smokeless: Prevention-persona RedFlag for smokeless tobacco. Most modifiable cancer exposure in users; cessation pharmacotherapy (nicotine replacement, varenicline) is effective. Oral examination at every encounter; biopsy any leukoplakia/erythroplakia >2 weeks; visual inspection with toluidine blue or autofluorescence in high-burden settings. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for sugar-swe: Prevention-persona RedFlag sokerilla makeutetun juoman tavanomaisesta nauttimisesta. Neuvoja: veden/makeuttamattomien juomien korvaaminen; pienentäminen asteittain, jos äkillinen lopettaminen on vaikeaa; painonnousun ja glykeemisen häiriöiden säätelyn arvioiminen. Vaatimaton yksilöllinen RR, mutta hyvin yleinen altistus → suuri absoluuttinen populaation osuus. STUB odottaa kahden kerroksen eroa CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode -menetelmää kohti.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for tamoxifen: Prevention-persona RedFlag for tamoxifen exposure ≥5y in women with intact uterus. ~2-7 fold endometrial cancer risk. Engine routes to PreventionPlan recommending symptom-prompted evaluation (postmenopausal bleeding → immediate workup with TVUS + endometrial biopsy). Routine asymptomatic TVUS screening NOT recommended per ACOG (false-positives from tamoxifen-related subepithelial changes). STUB pending two-Clinical-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for transplan: Ennaltaehkäisyhenkilö RedFlag elinsiirtojen immunosuppression hoitoon. Moottorireitit PreventionPlaniin tehoseurannalla + vähentää immunosruptiokeskustelua + kohdennettua seulontaa. STUB.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for type-2 di: Prevention-persona RedFlag for type-2 diabetes mellitus as multi-organ modest cancer risk amplifier. New-onset T2DM ≥50 with weight loss has ~1% absolute 3-year risk of pancreatic cancer — actionable surveillance signal (EUS or MR-pancreas in high-risk subset per ACG 2022). Other cancer-risk contributions are background and modify population-screening adherence rather than triggering off-schedule imaging. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff per CHARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for very hot: Ennaltaehkäisyhenkilö RedFlag erittäin kuuman juomankulutukseen ≥65 °C. IARC Group 2A -luokitus (2016). Merkityksellisintä alueilla, joilla on korkea tausta-alue ESCC-esiintyvyys (Iran, Turkki, Kiina, Etelä-Amerikan osat). Vaikutuskoko vaatimaton matalan riskin alueilla. Moottorireitit PreventionPlaniin suosittelevat juoman lämpötilaneuvontaa. STUB odottaa kahden klinikan ja yhtymän välistä eroa per CARTER §6.1 dev-mode.
Prevention-persona RedFlag for vinyl chl: Prevention-persona RedFlag vinyylikloridille → maksaangiosarkooma / HCC. Pre-1974 PVC:n työntekijät ovat edelleen jäännösriskissä. STUB odottaa kahden yhtiön johtajaa.
Prevention-persona RedFlag — v0.3 IARC 2: Prevention-persona RedFlag — v0.3 IARC 2A probable-carcinogen batch (2026-05-19). IARC Group 2A probable — limited human evidence; clinical recommendation more conservative than Group 1. IARC Monograph 112 (2015) is the canonical evidence anchor and is NOT yet a separate SRC entity in KB; cited in notes only. Evidence-base contestation: the IARC Group 2A classification is not concordant with EFSA / EPA / Health Canada / JMPR "unlikely to pose carcinogenic risk" conclusions. This RF is authored at severity:minor reflecting both the IARC 2A probable evidence quality AND the cross-regulatory disagreement. Counseling should disclose the controversy honestly rather than presenting IARC as settled science. Anchor scope: DLBCL only (the dominant NHL endpoint in IARC 112 limited-human-evidence summary). Other NHL subtypes (follicular, marginal zone, etc.) and other hematologic malignancies (MM, AML) carry inadequate or more-contested evidence and are deliberately excluded from relevant_diseases. Engine routes to 2-track PreventionPlan: (a) IND-OCC-GLYPHOSATE-PREVENTION-INTENSIFIED-SURVEILLANCE (standard) — symptom-awareness education, annual CBC, targeted lymphadenopathy / B-symptom histo...

KEYNOTE-158 (Shapira-Frommer, Gynecol Oncol 2022) evaluated pembrolizumab monotherapy in previously treated advanced vulvar SCC (n=101): durable responses (ORR 10.9% overall, median DOR 20.4 months among responders) occurred in BOTH PD-L1-positive (ORR 9.5%, n=84) and PD-L1-negative (ORR 28.6%, n=7 — small subgroup, wide CI) patients. Primary IO resistance is operationally d: Primary IO resistance is operationally distinct from acquired resistance (PD after initial response >6 months). SITC consensus (Kluger 2020) defines primary resistance as PD within 6 months of IO start. Subsequent options vary by tumor: melanoma — BRAF/MEKi if V600E, T-VEC, TIL therapy at trial centers, IL-2; NSCLC — docetaxel ± ramucirumab, ADC if HER2/TROP2; urothelial — enfortumab vedotin + pembrolizumab combination remains active even after IO-mono PD per EV-302; RCC — cabozantinib monotherapy or lenvatinib + everolimus. IO-rechallenge is generally not standard but may be considered after >6 months treatment-free + non-PD discontinuation reason.

Primary Sjögren's syndrome (chronic autoimmune exocrinopathy with characteristic anti-Ro/SSA ± anti-La/SSB autoantibodies and histologic focal lymphocytic infiltration of minor salivary glands; EULAR/ACR 2016 classification criteria) in an individual without a current lymphoma diagnosis. The strongest hematologic-cancer risk factor among rheumatic diseases — ~15-20x relative risk for marginal zone (MALT) lymphoma, predominantly arising in parotid and lacrimal glands, with lifetime incidence ~5-10%. Risk concentrated in patients with persistent parotid swelling, palpable purpura, cryoglobulinemia, low C4 complement, monoclonal gammopathy, lymph- node enlargement, or high EULAR Sjögren's Disease Activity Index (ESSDAI). Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) — confirmed by characteristic cholangiographic findings on MRCP or ERCP (multifocal intra-/extra- hepatic biliary strictures with intervening dilatation, beaded appearance) and/or liver biopsy (concentric periductal fibrosis, onion-skin pattern). Includes PSC-IBD subgroup (very high risk for both CRC and cholangiocarcinoma) and PSC with dominant biliary stricture (additional cholangiocarcinoma risk requiring focused diagnostic workup). No current cholangiocarcinoma, gallbladder cancer, or HCC diagnosis. PSC is the strongest known risk factor for cholangiocarcinoma — lifetime risk ~10-15% (vs ~0.01% in general population); annual incidence ~0.5-1.5% per year. Provides supplemental elemental calcium: Provides supplemental elemental calcium (~40% by mass of calcium carbonate). Absorbed in proximal small bowel via active vitamin-D- dependent transcellular transport (saturable at low calcium intake) and passive paracellular diffusion (linear with concentration). Cancer-prevention rationale: intraluminal calcium binds free bile acids and free fatty acids in the colon, reducing their proliferative and pro-inflammatory effect on colonic mucosa; additionally calcium modulates epithelial cell proliferation/differentiation via the calcium-sensing receptor. Calcium Polyp Prevention Study (Baron NEJM 1999) and follow-on trials: 1200 mg/day elemental calcium reduced metachronous adenoma recurrence by ~15-20%.

Pyrimidine analog. Intracellularly conve: Pyrimidine analog. Intracellularly converted to FdUMP, FdUTP, and FUTP. FdUMP forms a stable ternary complex with thymidylate synthase (TS) + reduced folate (leucovorin), depleting dTMP and blocking DNA synthesis. FUTP misincorporation into RNA disrupts pre-mRNA processing; FdUTP misincorporation into DNA produces strand breaks. Backbone of FOLFOX, FOLFIRI, FOLFIRINOX, FLOT, and capecitabine-bridged regimens. Bolus and continuous-infusion (CIV) schedules differ in toxicity profile (more myelosuppression with bolus, more mucositis/HFS with CIV).
Pyrimidine nucleoside analog incorporate: Pyrimidine nucleoside analog incorporated into DNA and RNA, inhibits DNA methyltransferases → re-expression of silenced tumor-suppressor genes + cytotoxicity at higher doses. Backbone of MDS-HR, AML-unfit (with venetoclax), and CMML 1L therapy.
Pyrimidine nucleoside analog of deoxycyt: Pyrimidine nucleoside analog of deoxycytidine. Phosphorylated by deoxycytidine kinase (rate-limiting) to active metabolites gemcitabine diphosphate (dFdCDP) and triphosphate (dFdCTP). dFdCDP inhibits ribonucleotide reductase, depleting deoxynucleotide pools required for DNA synthesis (self-potentiation effect — increases cellular dFdCTP). dFdCTP is incorporated into DNA, after which one additional natural nucleotide is added before DNA polymerase stalls — "masked chain termination" — making the lesion resistant to exonucleolytic repair. Cell cycle phase-specific (S phase) with G1/S blockade. PDAC backbone (gem-nab-pac MPACT, gem mono in frail), biliary tract cancers, NSCLC, bladder, NK/T-nasal lymphoma (SMILE), Hodgkin / DLBCL salvage (GDP).
Pyrrolopyrimidine antifolate that, after: Pyrrolopyrimidine antifolate that, after intracellular polyglutamation by folylpolyglutamate synthetase, simultaneously inhibits multiple folate-dependent enzymes critical for thymidine and purine biosynthesis: thymidylate synthase (TS — primary target), dihydrofolate reductase (DHFR), and glycinamide ribonucleotide formyltransferase (GARFT). The combined inhibition disrupts both thymidylate and purine de-novo synthesis, halting DNA / RNA production and producing S-phase-specific cytotoxicity. Activity is histology-restricted: highly active in non-squamous NSCLC and malignant pleural mesothelioma (MPM); minimal-to-no activity in squamous NSCLC due to higher baseline TS expression in squamous histology. R140Q is the dominant IDH2 hotspot in AM: R140Q is the dominant IDH2 hotspot in AML (~70-80% of IDH2-mut AML; ~6-8% of all AML). Enasidenib (IDHIFA, AG-221) FDA-approved Aug 2017 for R/R-AML-IDH2 monotherapy (phase 1/2: ORR 38%, CR 19%). 1L combination with azacitidine in unfit patients (AG221-AML-005: ORR 71%). Differentiation syndrome (~14%) — same monitoring + dexamethasone protocol as ivosidenib. Hyperbilirubinemia (~80% any grade; UGT1A1 inhibition — usually asymptomatic, no dose adjustment unless symptomatic). IDHENTIFY R/R AML phase-3 did not show OS benefit vs conventional care over all comers but enriched in IDH2-mut who had not received prior HMA. Combination with venetoclax + azacitidine under study. Triggers RF-AML-IDH2-MUT-ACTIONABLE (existing) for algorithm routing.
R172K is the second IDH2 hotspot in AML: R172K is the second IDH2 hotspot in AML (~20-30% of IDH2-mut AML; ~2-3% of all AML). Enasidenib (IDHIFA, AG-221) FDA-approved across both R140 and R172 variants. Glioma IDH2 R172K is a separate clinical entity (vorasidenib INDIGO trial) — this biomarker is AML-scoped; glioma IDH2 captured under BIO-IDH-MUTATION composite. Triggers RF-AML-IDH2-MUT-ACTIONABLE (existing) for algorithm routing.
R175H is the most common TP53 missense h: R175H is the most common TP53 missense hotspot across all human cancers (~5-7% of TP53-mutant tumors per IARC TP53 Database). Structural class mutant — the R175 substitution to histidine disrupts the DNA-binding domain fold (zinc-coordination region). Beyond loss-of-function (LoF), R175H is a canonical example of mutant-p53 GAIN-OF-FUNCTION (GOF): the mutant protein acquires pro-oncogenic activities (chemoresistance via NF-kB, increased migration/invasion, metabolic reprogramming, chronic inflammation). Clinical implication: R175H+ tumors generally have worse chemo response than TP53-WT or even other TP53-mut tumors. In AML: TP53-mut (any) including R175H → very poor outcomes with intensive chemo, route to alloSCT or venetoclax-azacitidine + clinical trials. In MM: routes to quadruplet per high-risk cytogenetics composite. Emerging GOF-targeting strategies (eprenetapopt/APR-246, arsenic trioxide for structural mutants) are largely investigational; R175H specifically among the reactivatable structural mutants.
R248 is one of the six most-mutated codo: R248 is one of the six most-mutated codons in TP53 (along with R175, G245, R249, R273, R282). DNA-contact class: R248 sits in the L3 loop and makes direct base-specific contact with the DNA minor groove. Substitution to glutamine (R248Q) abolishes sequence-specific DNA binding while preserving overall fold (distinguishing it from structural R175H). R248Q has well-documented gain-of-function (GOF) activities in mouse models — accelerates tumorigenesis and metastasis beyond simple p53-null. Clinical implications mirror other TP53 hotspots: in AML/MDS routes away from intensive chemo toward venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT; in CLL/MCL/MM contraindicates chemoimmuno or routes to high-risk-cytogenetics regimens. Distinction from R248W (different substitution, also a hotspot) — R248Q tends to retain partial folding while R248W more disruptive; both are pathogenic.
R273 is among the top three most-mutated: R273 is among the top three most-mutated TP53 codons (with R175 and R248). DNA-contact class: R273 directly contacts the DNA major groove via its guanidinium side chain. R→H substitution preserves the thermal stability of the protein fold (distinguishing it from structural R175H) but eliminates specific DNA binding. R273H is one of the best-characterized GOF p53 mutants — promotes chemoresistance via NF-κB activation, drives invasion/metastasis through CXCR4 and RhoA pathways, reprograms metabolism (mevalonate pathway upregulation). Clinical implications mirror the TP53-mutant class: AML/MDS — venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT consideration; CLL/MCL — contraindicates chemoimmuno; MM — high-risk cytogenetics composite routes to quadruplet. Notably, R273H tumors are particularly resistant to platinum chemotherapy across solid-tumor types per multiple correlative analyses — relevant for ovarian, lung, esophageal cancer treatment selection.
R282 is the sixth most-mutated TP53 codo: R282 is the sixth most-mutated TP53 codon, often grouped with R248 and R273 as the canonical hotspot ring. Hybrid structural/contact mutant: R282 stabilizes the L1/S3 loop region adjacent to the DNA-binding surface, and R→W partially destabilizes the fold while altering contact geometry. Functional studies show R282W retains partial transactivation activity on a subset of canonical p53 targets (CDKN1A/p21, BBC3/PUMA at reduced levels) — termed "partial LoF" — while still gaining oncogenic activities. Clinically R282W behaves similarly to other hotspots: in AML/MDS poor chemo response → routes to venetoclax-azacitidine + alloSCT consideration; in CLL/MCL/MM high-risk regimen routing. Distinction from full LoF mutants (truncating, splice-site) may matter for emerging mutant-p53 reactivator drugs (eprenetapopt) where residual fold is required — R282W generally considered reactivatable in early-phase trials.

RB1 alterations (deletion, mutation) occur in ~30% of muscle-invasive bladder cancer (MIBC) and are enriched in the basal/squamous-differentiated molecular subtype (~50%). RB1 loss is associated with resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors (which require pRb to exert G1 arrest). In urothelial cancer, CDK4/6 inhibitors are investigational (no approved indication); however, RB1 status is being evaluated as a predictive biomarker for CDK4/6 inhibitor non-response in HR+ cancers where bladder patients are enrolled in basket trials. Therapeutic implications in bladder cancer: (1) RB1 loss may associate with sensitivity to immunotherapy (higher genomic instability) — inconsistent evidence; (2) Basal/squamous subtype (often RB1-low) responds better to neoadjuvant chemotherapy than luminal subtypes; (3) No approved targeted therapy exploits RB1 deficiency in bladder cancer as of 2026. ESCAT IIIB: RB1 is a prognostic and potential therapeutic vulnerability marker in urothelial cancer; no approved targeted agent.

RB1 biallelic loss, together with TP53 loss, is the molecular hallmark of SCLC (~95% of cases have both). RB1 loss is not used to select therapy in SCLC (all SCLC patients receive the same backbone: EP/EC ± atezolizumab/durvalumab); rather, it is a diagnostic characteristic and potential therapeutic vulnerability. RB1 loss renders cells dependent on alternative cell cycle regulators (CDK4/6-independent E2F activation) — this is why CDK4/6 inhibitors have no activity in SCLC (pRb loss negates CDK4/6 inhibition). Investigational targeting of RB1-deficient SCLC: aurora kinase A inhibitors (alisertib — phase II, limited activity); EZH2 inhibitors (tazemetostat — RB1-null tumors may have heightened EZH2 dependence); LSD1 inhibitors; ATR/CHK1 inhibitors (replication stress in RB1-null context). ESCAT IIIB: RB1 loss is diagnostically informative and a conceptual therapeutic target, but no FDA-approved targeted therapy exploiting RB1 deficiency as of 2026.
RB1 encodes the retinoblastoma protein (: RB1 encodes the retinoblastoma protein (pRb), the master G1/S checkpoint regulator. pRb normally sequesters E2F transcription factors to prevent S-phase entry; loss of pRb → uncontrolled cell cycle progression. Clinical contexts: (1) Hereditary retinoblastoma: germline RB1 mutation → bilateral/multifocal retinoblastoma in childhood; lifetime elevated risk of osteosarcoma, SCLC, melanoma. (2) SCLC: biallelic RB1 loss + TP53 mutation defines the SCLC molecular signature (~95% of SCLC). pRb loss by IHC is used in pathologic diagnosis. No targeted therapy for RB1 deficiency per se; SCLC treatment is chemotherapy (EP/EC) ± atezolizumab. (3) Urothelial carcinoma: RB1 alterations in ~30% of muscle-invasive bladder cancer; associated with basal/squamous subtype; not currently targeted. (4) Breast cancer: RB1 mutations occur in ~10% of TNBC; RB1 loss predicts resistance to CDK4/6 inhibitors (palbociclib, ribociclib, abemaciclib) — pRb is the substrate for CDK4/6 that drives cell cycle entry; without pRb, CDK4/6 inhibition is ineffective. RB1 germline pathogenic variants cause heritable retinoblastoma (~40% of retinoblastoma cases) — bilateral / multifocal disease in 80% of carriers, median age at diagnosis ~12 months. Carriers face lifetime ~50% risk of secondary primary cancers (osteosarcoma, soft-tissue sarcoma, melanoma, lung, bladder); cumulative risk markedly elevated after external-beam radiation therapy (EBRT) — modern protocols avoid EBRT to mitigate. Confirmed-carrier surveillance protocol (per COG / Children's Oncology Group + International Retinoblastoma Consortium): pediatric ophthalmology with EUA (examination under anesthesia) starting in newborn period — every 2-4 weeks until age 1, then progressive lengthening to monthly → q3mo → q6mo through age 7, annual through adolescence. Cascade testing to all first-degree relatives mandatory. Lifelong secondary-cancer surveillance: annual skin exam, attentiveness to bone pain (osteosarcoma in adolescence/young adulthood), avoidance of unnecessary diagnostic ionizing radiation. ESCAT IIA.

Surveillance: ophthalmologic exam under anaesthesia every 1-3 months in infancy; long-term sarcoma surveillance. STUB pending two-Co-Lead signoff.

RET mutations are the defining oncogenic driver of hereditary and sporadic MTC: approximately 25% of sporadic MTC carry somatic RET mutations (M918T in ~50% of these), and hereditary MTC (Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2A/2B, Familial MTC) is driven by germline RET mutations (C634R/W/Y/F in MEN2A; M918T in MEN2B; C611/C620/C630 in FMTC-risk MEN2A kindreds). Radiotherapy contraindicated or declined for early-stage NLPBL (nodular lymphocyte-predominant B-cell lymphoma, WHO 5th ed). Major clinical scenarios: (1) Young patient with breast or thyroid field overlap — cumulative RT dose risk of secondary malignancy and cardiac toxicity unacceptable; (2) Prior RT to the involved or adjacent region — reirradiation risks exceed benefit; (3) Patient refuses RT after informed discussion. In all scenarios rituximab monotherapy (4–8 × R weekly) achieves ~94% ORR with ≥70% CR in early-stage NLPBL (Advani 2014, IELSG-37 data) and is the accepted standard alternative. RT remains the default for eligible patients where field is safe and patient consents (stage IA-IIA, ≤2 cm).

Rare but tumor-agnostic actionable drive: Rare but tumor-agnostic actionable driver. Highest prevalence in invasive mucinous adenocarcinoma of lung (~7-27% of KRAS-WT IMA), pancreatic KRAS-WT (~3-5%), and isolated cholangio / breast / sarcoma cases. Zenocutuzumab (Bizengri, MCLA-128) — first-in-class HER2 × HER3 bispecific IgG1 — granted FDA accelerated approval 4 Dec 2024 for advanced unresectable / metastatic NSCLC and pancreatic cancer with NRG1 fusion who progressed on prior systemic therapy. eNRGy phase-2 trial (n=204): ORR 33% NSCLC, 42% pancreatic; mDOR ~7-9 mo. Pan-tumor approval reflects rarity (no head-to-head alternative). RNA-NGS testing critical — fusion missed by DNA-only panels in 30-40% of cases. Clinical practice gap: most KRAS-WT pancreatic / IMA-NSCLC patients still not tested at progression. Trial-Source SRC-ENRGY-SCHRAM-2024 not yet ingested — flag for ingestion chunk.

Rd continuous (lenalidomide + low-dose d: Rd continuous (lenalidomide + low-dose dexamethasone until progression) was the MAIA control arm (Facon NEJM 2019, PMID 30926586) and represents the standard-access first-line regimen for transplant-ineligible NDMM. MAIA control arm outcomes: ORR 75.8%, PFS HR (D-Rd vs Rd) 0.56 (95% CI 0.43–0.73), 30-month PFS ~53.3% for D-Rd vs ~37.8% for Rd. Rd continuous showed superiority over MPT and melphalan-prednisone in the FIRST trial (Benboubker NEJM 2014, PMID 25184863): PFS 26 months vs 21.9 months for MPT. Dose of dexamethasone: low-dose (40 mg weekly = "Ld schedule") is preferred over high-dose (480 mg/cycle); ECOG E4A03 showed equivalent efficacy and better tolerability with low-dose dex in NDMM (Rajkumar LANCET ONCOL 2010). Renal adjustment is critical: lenalidomide is ~80% renally cleared. CrCl 30-60 → 10 mg daily; CrCl <30 → 5 mg daily or 10 mg qod. Myeloma renal impairment often improves with therapy — recheck CrCl monthly and escalate dose when GFR recovers. Second primary malignancy (SPM) risk: CALGB 100104 and IFM 2005-02 documented elevated SPM (MDS/AML) with lenalidomide maintenance post-ASCT; risk applies to continuous Rd as well at smaller magnitude. Recombinant humanized IgG1 monoclonal an: Recombinant humanized IgG1 monoclonal antibody binding all isoforms of vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGF-A) in plasma and extracellular space, preventing VEGF-A from engaging VEGFR-1 (Flt-1) and VEGFR-2 (KDR) on vascular endothelium. Net effects: inhibition of tumor angiogenesis, regression of existing tumor microvasculature, and transient vessel normalization improving drug delivery. Adds approximately 2-4 months PFS in metastatic CRC when added to FOLFOX/FOLFIRI; combined with atezolizumab in 1L unresectable HCC (IMbrave150) and with chemo in NSCLC, ovarian, cervical. Class effects (HTN, proteinuria, bleeding, perforation) derive from systemic VEGF blockade.
Recombinant non-infectious bivalent HPV: Recombinant non-infectious bivalent HPV vaccine. Each dose contains virus-like particles (VLPs) assembled from the L1 major capsid protein of two HPV types — 16 and 18 — produced in a baculovirus expression system in Trichoplusia ni insect cells (Hi-5) and adjuvanted with AS04 (3-O-desacyl-4'-monophosphoryl lipid A on aluminium hydroxide), a TLR4 agonist designed to enhance and prolong the antibody response. L1 VLPs contain no viral DNA — cannot cause HPV infection. Vaccination elicits high-titer neutralizing IgG against HPV 16 and 18; cross- neutralization against types 31, 33, 45, 58 is documented (modest efficacy, lower than direct protection). Cancer-prevention pathway: prevents persistent infection with HPV 16 and 18 — responsible for ~70% of cervical cancers, ~80% of anal cancers, ~85% of HPV-related oropharyngeal cancers globally. Recombinant non-infectious nine-valent H: Recombinant non-infectious nine-valent HPV vaccine. Each dose contains virus-like particles (VLPs) assembled from the L1 major capsid protein of nine HPV types — 6, 11, 16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52, and 58 — produced in Saccharomyces cerevisiae and adjuvanted with amorphous aluminium hydroxyphosphate sulfate (AAHS). L1 VLPs are immunogenic but contain no viral DNA — cannot cause HPV infection. Vaccination elicits high-titer neutralizing IgG that prevents incident infection by the covered HPV types. Cancer-prevention pathway: prevents persistent infection with the HPV types responsible for ~90% of cervical cancers, ~90% of anal cancers, ~70% of vaginal/vulvar cancers, ~60% of penile cancers, and a growing fraction of oropharyngeal cancers.
Recombinant non-infectious vaccine conta: Recombinant non-infectious vaccine containing hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) produced in Saccharomyces cerevisiae (Engerix-B, Recombivax HB) or in mammalian cells (PreHevbrio — tri-antigen S/preS1/ preS2). Adjuvanted with aluminium hydroxide (Engerix-B, Recombivax HB), CpG 1018 toll-like receptor 9 agonist (Heplisav-B, two-dose adult schedule), or aluminium hydroxide + emulsion (PreHevbrio). HBsAg contains no viral DNA — cannot cause HBV infection. Vaccination elicits high-titer anti-HBs neutralizing IgG that prevents incident HBV infection on exposure. CANCER-PREVENTION PATHWAY: chronic HBV infection is responsible for ~50% of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) globally and a subset of HBV-associated B-cell non-Hodgkin lymphomas; preventing chronic HBV via vaccination is the single most effective primary- prevention intervention for HCC (WHO + IARC).

References BIO-AR-AMPLIFICATION. Detecti: References BIO-AR-AMPLIFICATION. Detection: ctDNA NGS (Guardant360, FoundationOne Liquid CDx) is the practical platform — tumor biopsy in mCRPC frequently fails (bone-only disease, low cellularity). Co-occurring resistance markers include AR-V7 splice variant, AR LBD point mutations (L702H, T878A, F877L), and lineage plasticity (neuroendocrine transformation). Priority 76 chosen to fall just below RF-PROSTATE-AR-V7-ARSI-RESISTANCE (75) — both are informational and complementary; AR-V7 evidence (PROPHECY) prospectively validated, AR-amp evidence largely retrospective ctDNA cohorts. KB scope choice: ships as biomarker + RF (informational) only — no new IND, no algorithm step. Tx-modifying signal deferred to a future taxane-mCRPC IND chunk that branches on AR-amp / AR-V7 / LBD-mutation status.

Regular processed-meat consumption ≥50 g: Regular processed-meat consumption ≥50 g/day per WCRF/IARC threshold. IARC Monograph 114 (2015) classified processed meat as Group 1 carcinogen for colorectal cancer (sufficient evidence). Each 50 g/day of processed meat increases CRC risk by ~18% (meta-analyzed RR ~1.18; WCRF/AICR convincing-evidence rating). Processed meat = sausages, ham, bacon, salami, cured/smoked/salted/preserved meat. Red meat (Group 2A per IARC, probable carcinogen) is a separate but overlapping concern — threshold ≥500 g/week for red meat. Mechanisms: N-nitroso compounds, heterocyclic amines, polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons, heme iron. Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 lifestyle pilot).

Pivotal data NP30179 phase 1/2 (Dickinson 2022 NEJM): ORR 52%, CR 39%, mPFS 4.9 mo, mDOR 18.4 mo in 3L+ R/R DLBCL after fixed treatment course. Differentiator vs epcoritamab: fixed-duration (12 cycles ≈ 8.3 mo) vs continuous; IV vs SC; obinutuzumab pre-treatment 7 days before C1D1 reduces CRS. Off-the-shelf alternative to CAR-T. Often considered after epcoritamab failure in BiTE-sequencing strategies, though direct comparative data are lacking.

Reproductive history combining late first full-term pregnancy (age ≥30) OR nulliparity, AND short cumulative lifetime breastfeeding duration (<6 months total). Both factors independently confer modest increases in hormone-receptor-positive breast cancer risk (RR ~1.2-1.4 each) per Collaborative Group on Hormonal Factors in Breast Cancer + WCRF/AICR. Breastfeeding is protective in dose- dependent fashion (~4% breast cancer risk reduction per 12 months of cumulative breastfeeding). Mechanism: cumulative ovulatory cycles + unopposed estrogen exposure + delayed terminal differentiation of breast ductal epithelium. Effect cumulative with other reproductive factors (early menarche, late menopause, nulliparity, HRT). Prevention-persona RedFlag (§20 v0.3 reproductive pilot).

Reserve antibiotic — escalation choice i: Reserve antibiotic — escalation choice in febrile neutropenia after 72-96 hours of empirical pip-tazo or cefepime without clinical improvement, and first-line for documented or strongly suspected MDR Gram-negative infection (ESBL Enterobacterales, AmpC overproducers, Pseudomonas with broad resistance). Antimicrobial stewardship critical: prolonged carbapenem use selects for carbapenem-resistant organisms (KPC, NDM, OXA-48). CRITICAL interaction: meropenem dramatically reduces valproate levels (60-100% drop within hours) — patients on valproate for seizures or mood stabilization need a switch to levetiracetam BEFORE meropenem start, with overlap of 2-3 days. Lower seizure risk than imipenem, but still elevated with renal dysfunction and CNS pathology — meticulous renal dosing required. Avoid in uncomplicated indications where pip-tazo or cefepime suffices. Ukraine: widely available, NSZU-covered for critical infections.
